title: Numbers in English words
prompt: Read lines from standard input, each an integer written as an optional minus sign and decimal digits (spaces at the start and end are ignored; empty lines are skipped). For each line print the number in English words, in lowercase: `zero`, `one`, ..., `nineteen`, `twenty`, `thirty`, `forty`, `fifty`, `sixty`, `seventy`, `eighty`, `ninety`; tens and units joined by a hyphen (`twenty-one`, `ninety-nine`); `one hundred`, `two hundred five`; groups separated by `thousand` and `million` (`one thousand`, `twelve thousand three hundred forty-five`, `one million`). No `and`, no commas. A negative number starts with `minus`. Print `invalid` for a line that is not an integer of that shape, or whose absolute value is above 999999999 (leading zeros are allowed: `007` is `seven`; `-0` is `zero`).
